tasks.title: Create Shared Resolver Infrastructure
tasks.description: Build the shared name-to-ID resolver framework in cmd/resolve.go that all new commands will use. This is foundational infrastructure that enables human-friendly identifiers across all domains.
tasks.details:
Create `cmd/resolve.go` with resolver functions for each entity type:

1. Define a `ResolverCache` struct with maps for teams, users, projects, states, etc. Instantiate per-command invocation.

2. Implement these resolver functions:
   - `ResolveTeam(client, keyOrID) (teamID, error)` - accepts team key (uppercase) or UUID
   - `ResolveUser(client, emailOrNameOrID) (userID, error)` - uses existing UserFilter with Or pattern
   - `ResolveProject(client, nameOrID) (projectID, error)` - case-insensitive name match via ProjectFilter
   - `ResolveWorkflowState(client, teamID, nameOrID) (stateID, error)` - uses embedded team.states.nodes
   - `ResolveInitiative(client, nameOrID) (initiativeID, error)` - new, uses InitiativeFilter
   - `ResolveCycle(client, teamID, numberOrNameOrID) (cycleID, error)` - number or name within team
   - `ResolveLabel(client, teamID, nameOrID) (labelID, error)` - team or workspace scope
   - `ResolveMilestone(client, projectID, nameOrID) (milestoneID, error)` - within project scope

3. Each resolver:
   - Returns input unchanged if it matches UUID pattern (regex `^[a-f0-9]{8}-`)
   - Caches lookups in the command-scoped cache
   - Case-insensitive comparison for names
   - Returns error with candidate list on ambiguous match: `fmt.Errorf("Multiple matches for '%s': %s", name, candidateList)`
   - Returns error with valid options on no match for bounded sets

4. Add helper `isUUID(s string) bool` using regex.

5. Refactor existing resolvers in cmd/issue.go (user, team, state, project lookups) to use the new shared helpers.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Unit test each resolver with mock data: UUID passthrough, exact name match, ambiguous names, not found cases.
2. Integration test: Verify existing issue update commands still work with --assignee, --state, --project flags.
3. Run full smoke_test.sh to confirm no regressions.
4. Manual verification: `lincli issue update SD-123 --assignee shane.dolley@email.com` and `lincli issue update SD-123 --state 'In Progress'`

```graphql
mutation UpdateInitiative($id: String!, $input: InitiativeUpdateInput!)  # Go name distinct from query

mutation InitiativeUnarchive($id: String!)

```

**Commands (cmd/initiative.go):**
- `initiative list` with --limit, --sort, --newer-than (default all_time), --include-archived
- `initiative get <id>` with Projects, Labels, Relations sections
- `initiative create --name (required) --description --owner --target-date --status`

- `initiative archive/unarchive/delete <id>`
- `initiative set-lead <id> --team --mode` (selectedOnly|includeDescendants)
- Nested group `initiative project`: add/remove/reorder

- `initiative relate <id> <other> --relation <kind> --remove`
- `initiative update-post`: list/create/edit/archive/unarchive

- Validate --status against InitiativeStatus enum: Proposed, Planned, Active, Completed, Canceled
- Validate --health against InitiativeUpdateHealthType: onTrack, atRisk, offTrack
- Validate --mode against InitiativeLeadTeamChangeMode: selectedOnly, includeDescendants
- --target-date accepts YYYY-MM-DD format
- Use ResolveInitiative from task 1 for name-to-ID
- Three-mode output (table/json/plaintext) matching existing patterns
